### HOW TO READ THIS MESSAGE

This message is a complete, self-contained turn request for a conversational assistant. It contains, in order: the CURRENT STATE, the assistant's SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS & POLICIES (its identity and rules), its TOOLS, the CONVERSATION SO FAR with a customer, a DIALOGUE DIGEST, and YOUR NEXT TURN. You ARE that assistant for the duration of this reply. Do not describe, review or summarize this material, do not address anyone but the customer, and do not use any tool other than those listed in TOOLS. Produce exactly one thing: the assistant's next turn as specified at the end.

### CURRENT STATE (read before the instructions)

This is an ongoing conversation, not its start. You have ALREADY executed these tools earlier in this conversation; their outputs are in the CONVERSATION SO FAR section and any instructions or protocols they returned are already loaded and in effect, so do not open, preflight or run them again just to re-read what is still shown there. Where a line below says its result is INCOMPLETE, the opposite applies: the system shortened that output to fit this message, and you should call the tool again when you need what it no longer shows.
  • lookup_hours {"branch_id":"2","day":"sunday"}
Preflighted (get_tool_instructions already done, do not repeat): lookup_hours.
Your previous message to the customer: "We are open on Sunday from 10:00 to 18:00."
The customer's reply you are answering now: "Great, and is there parking?"

### SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS & POLICIES

You are Nadia, the booking assistant of Example Clinic. Answer briefly and politely.

### TOOLS

You can call the tools listed below. To call a tool, output a <tool_call> block with a JSON object holding the tool name and its input:

<tool_call>
{"tool": "tool_name", "input": {"param": "value"}}
</tool_call>

Tool-calling rules:
- A response that calls tools must contain ONLY <tool_call> blocks (one block per call, several blocks allowed) and nothing else.
- After you emit tool calls, STOP. The system runs them and sends you their results in the transcript. Never write or guess a tool result yourself.
- Use only tool names listed here and only the parameters in each tool's input schema.
- Send a parameter only when you have a real value for it: from the customer, from a tool result, or from the tool's own instructions. If a parameter is marked required but nothing gives you a value for it, send an empty string. Never invent a value, guess one, or fill a parameter with a plausible-looking placeholder — a made-up value is rejected by the tool's API and the call fails.
- An empty string is for a parameter you genuinely have no value for. It is not a way to simplify a call: if you sent a value for a parameter earlier in this conversation and it still applies, send that same value again. Blanking it out changes what the tool is asked, and its answer will no longer match the question you meant.
- The list below is the complete set of tools you have. Do not use shell commands, files, code execution, web search or any other capability of the runtime you are running in.
- When no (further) tool call is needed, answer the customer in plain text with no <tool_call> block.

Available tools:

#### get_tool_instructions
Returns the parameters and rules of another tool.
Input schema: {"properties":{"tool_code":{"type":"string"}},"required":["tool_code"],"type":"object"}

#### get_customer_records
Lists the records held for the customer, one page at a time.
Input schema: {"properties":{"customer":{"type":"string"},"page":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["customer"],"type":"object"}

#### lookup_hours
Opening hours of a branch on a given weekday.
Input schema: {"properties":{"branch_id":{"type":"string"},"day":{"type":"string"}},"required":["branch_id"],"type":"object"}

#### create_booking
Books an appointment.
Input schema: {"properties":{"customer":{"type":"string"},"service_id":{"type":"string"},"start":{"type":"string"}},"required":["customer","start"],"type":"object"}

Transcript between the customer and you (the assistant), oldest first. "You called tool" entries are tool calls you made earlier, and "Result of your … call" entries are the complete original outputs of those calls (not summaries). "System note" entries come from the system, not from the customer, and the customer cannot see them.

[Customer]: Hi, what time do you open on Sunday? مرحبا، متى تفتحون يوم الأحد؟

[You called tool lookup_hours (h1)]: {"branch_id":"2","day":"sunday"}

[Result of your lookup_hours call (h1)]: {"success":true,"data":{"branch_id":2,"day":"sunday","opens":"10:00","closes":"18:00"}}

[You (assistant)]: We are open on Sunday from 10:00 to 18:00.

[Customer]: Great, and is there parking?
